review_candidates.title: Director of Customer Success
review_candidates.description: The role We’re looking for a senior, hands-on leader to own the success and operational performance of a diverse portfolio of clients. The role brings together customer success, commercial ownership and operations . You’ll work close enough to clients to understand what drives their success, connect patterns across the portfolio, and turn those insights into changes in how we onboard, deliver, organise teams and use technology. Our service model is evolving across people-led, technology-enabled and AI-supported services. You’ll need to operate effectively in that ambiguity: run what exists today, challenge what isn’t working, and build better ways of operating as we learn. You’ll be equally comfortable getting deep into an individual client problem and stepping back to ask what it tells us about the broader system. What you’ll own Client and portfolio performance. Understand what clients need, identify patterns and intervene where customer outcomes, retention or economics need to change. Operational delivery and improvement. Keep day-to-day delivery moving while improving the processes, systems and ways of working behind it. Commercial performance. Understand customer value, cost to serve, retention and margin, and use that perspective to make better client and operational decisions. Scalability and technology. Challenge complexity, handoffs and manual work. Use better process, systems, automation and AI to solve problems and support scale. Client onboarding and growth readiness. Work across Growth, Delivery and HR to make onboarding repeatable and ensure workforce, hiring and capacity plans anticipate demand. Organisation and capability. Design the organisation around what the portfolio needs, select and develop strong people, build leverage through your team, and question structures that no longer fit. Cross-functional execution. Work across Growth, HR, Product, Technology and senior leadership to resolve dependencies and move decisions into action. What we're looking for We’re open-minded about where you’ve built your experience. You might come from Customer Success, Customer Operations, managed services, technology-enabled services, scale-up operations, Business Operations or BPO/service delivery. The common thread we're looking for is end-to-end ownership . You've had to understand a customer or business problem, understand what's really causing it, decide what to do, implement the change and live with the consequences. We’re looking for: Critical thinking and judgement. You absorb complex and sometimes contradictory information, find the signal and reach a view without waiting for perfect information. Ownership and pace. You take problems through to resolution, keep things moving and close loops. Operational depth. You understand how work actually gets done and can move comfortably between the detail and the bigger system. Commercial judgement. You understand customer value, retention, cost and margin and can make sensible trade-offs between them. Systems thinking. You connect individual problems to broader patterns and redesign the underlying process or system where needed. Technology fluency. You are comfortable using modern systems, automation and AI and can see practical opportunities to apply them to operations. Influence. You can absorb different perspectives, challenge constructively, make a persuasive case and create alignment across functions. People judgement and organisation design. You can assess capability, select and develop people, delegate meaningful ownership and design teams around the work that needs to be done. Leadership experience. You’ve managed senior individual contributors or a team of leaders. Experience managing managers is highly advantageous. BPO or outsourced customer service experience is useful, but not required. Product experience is also useful, particularly if you've worked at the intersection of customer problems and service design. We care more about the quality and complexity of the problems you’ve owned than the size of the organisation you’ve managed. This role may suit you if... You like getting to the bottom of messy problems and making sense of competing signals. You can spend one hour working through the economics and customer experience of an individual account, then use what you learned to question something about the broader operating model. You naturally look for patterns. When the same problem appears twice, you want to understand what in the system is allowing it to happen. You make decisions, test ideas and adjust as you learn. Ambiguity doesn't become a reason to leave decisions sitting unresolved. You enjoy building through people while remaining a strong individual contributor yourself. Why Influx Influx provides customer support for brands and technology companies around the world, 24/7. We’re a fully remote, global company , with more than 1,000 people working across 15+ countries. This role is based in Indonesia, working with colleagues and clients across multiple countries, cultures and time zones. You'll have: Genuine global exposure , working across an international client portfolio and distributed teams. Fully remote work from Indonesia , in a company that has operated remotely for more than a decade. Broad scope and meaningful ownership , spanning clients, operations, commercial performance, people and technology. Direct access to senior leaders and the opportunity to influence decisions across Delivery, Growth, HR, Product and Technology. Room to shape how we operate , as our service models continue to evolve across people, technology and AI. If you enjoy owning complex customer and operational problems and turning what you learn into practical change, we’d like to hear from you.

We are looking for a Chief of Staff to the CEO to take ownership of some of the most important and difficult problems in the company. This is not an Executive Assistant role and it is not primarily about managing the CEO’s schedule or coordinating meetings. You will work directly with the CEO on problems that cut across functions and do not have an obvious owner yet. That could mean evaluating a new market, driving a strategic customer opportunity, preparing for a fundraise, fixing an operational bottleneck, recruiting a critical hire, structuring a new partnership, or building a process from scratch. The common thread is simple: the problem matters, it is ambiguous, and someone needs to own it end to end. What you’ll do Take ownership of high-priority problems across the company Turn loosely defined goals into concrete plans and execution Work on strategy, fundraising, business development, recruiting, operations, and new initiatives Drive projects that cut across multiple teams and functions Build analysis and recommendations for important company decisions Work directly with customers, investors, partners, and candidates Identify bottlenecks and solve them before they slow the company down Create structure where there is none Step into problems that are important but do not fit neatly into an existing role Follow through until the result is delivered What we’re looking for We are looking for people with unusually strong judgment, ownership, and problem-solving ability. You should be able to take a problem you have never seen before, understand it quickly, figure out what matters, and move it forward without needing a detailed set of instructions. You are likely a good fit if you: Think clearly and independently Learn new domains quickly Have strong analytical judgment Write and communicate well Can move between strategy and execution Are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information Take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks Can work with founders, engineers, customers, investors, and operators Have high standards for your own work Are comfortable being measured by the quality of the problems you solve We care much more about ability and trajectory than a specific background. You may come from startups, investing, consulting, engineering, technology, manufacturing, defense, or somewhere else entirely. Korean and English fluency is strongly preferred. Compensation This is a high-expectation, high-ownership role. Compensation will reflect the level of responsibility, judgment, and complexity we expect from the person taking it on. For the right person, we are prepared to pay competitively and structure meaningful upside. Why this role You will have direct exposure to the major decisions involved in building F4GE and substantial room to take ownership as the company grows. This role can become much bigger than a traditional Chief of Staff position. We are looking for someone who wants to become one of the people the company can trust with its hardest problems.
